source.title: The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics
source.authors: Soufiane Hayou; Nikhil Ghosh; Bin Yu

record.file_problem: The full text is present. Some PDF text extraction is garbled in the figures, but the relevant prose and reported metrics are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports LoRA fine-tuning results comparing two adapter initializations, but it does not test any listed version's training-error, bad-local-minimum, plain-network depth, matched activation initialization, above-stability learning-rate, or batch-normalization claim.
record.gate_note: The study's results concern pretrained models fine-tuned with LoRA and report test accuracy or perplexity, plus feature magnitudes and synthetic-model loss. None measures training classification error from random initialization on the benchmarks named in the claim. The paper also discusses its own LoRA feature-stability and feature-learning definitions, which are not measures named by the versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares LoRA factor initializations in pretrained language models and a synthetic residual model. Its task metrics, feature magnitudes and synthetic regression losses do not test V1–V6. In particular, V4 concerns activation-matched initialization and signal propagation across depth in plain networks; V5 concerns loss and curvature dynamics relative to a stability threshold. Neither is measured here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors favor Init[A], which generally permits larger optimal learning rates and better empirical performance. Their theory identifies internal feature growth with Init[A] and undertraining of B with Init[B], so both schemes have asymptotic shortcomings. Their data-agnostic feature-learning analysis does not establish generalization effects.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares two LoRA factor initializations during pretrained-model fine-tuning and evaluates task performance and feature dynamics; it does not use the original claim's from-scratch benchmark classification-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported best performance and optimal learning rate vary by task and initialization; for QNLI and Llama-7b on Flan-v2, the optimal learning rates were the same across the tested grid, despite reported performance differences.

fits_no_version.finding: Init[A] gives better reported downstream metrics than Init[B] on all six tested language-model tasks; optimal learning rates are larger on some tasks and equal on others.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly initializing A and zeroing B generally improves the tested LoRA fine-tuning outcomes compared with the reverse initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic model shows larger internal feature magnitudes with Init[A] at large width and lower or equal displayed training losses in Figure 3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA initialization changes internal feature dynamics and attainable training loss in the tested synthetic setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–2 derive different width scalings for output-stable learning rates: n^-1/2 for Init[A] and n^-1 for Init[B], under the stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA factor initialization determines asymptotic learning-rate scaling and a tradeoff between internal feature stability and efficient feature updates.

record.problems: The paper says its feature-learning analysis is data-agnostic and cannot establish generalization effects. Some empirical comparisons average over only two seeds; RoBERTa comparisons use three seeds. Reported test metrics do not establish training classification error. The toy figure's numeric train-loss values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result relevant to the listed claim versions was omitted. The paper gives additional plots and heatmaps, but their outcomes concern LoRA initialization, feature magnitude, or task metrics rather than the versions' specified measures.

untested.parts: From-scratch convolutional training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and recipe-dependent failures.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student models and their removal by one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation across depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep plain tanh training and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients across depth; resulting training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, threshold-tracking sharpness and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The edge-of-stability comparison in Section 3.5 is an analogy concerning bounded features as width grows, not a measurement of V5's temporal loss and sharpness dynamics. All row states describe inability to determine a listed version, rather than absence of the paper's LoRA effects.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error from random initialization; CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; model size, training duration, early stopping, and regularization effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional network training error across depth; special initialization of very deep plain tanh networks; residual training without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization in plain networks, training speed and trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Training above the stability limit, loss rise and recovery, sharpness at the stability threshold, and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual training without normalization.

rows.subject: Roberta-Large
rows.operation_detail: Compared Init[A] and Init[B] LoRA adapter initializations during fine-tuning; reports best test accuracy.
rows.note: The paper describes the difference as significant and says the values are over 3 random seeds. This is test accuracy after pretrained-model fine-tuning, not training classification error from random initialization.
rows.check: Reported accuracies are correct, but measure downstream test performance after LoRA fine-tuning.

rows.check: Reported perplexities are correct. A larger optimal learning rate does not establish recovery above an initial stability threshold.

rows.value: The text states that train loss is consistently smaller with Init[A]; numeric values are figure-only.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative train-loss comparison in prose; the figure's numeric labels are not sufficiently recoverable. This result does not measure a listed claim-version outcome.
rows.check: Split feature magnitudes and training loss into separate measures. Figure 3 supplies readable training losses: Init[A] versus Init[B] is 4.2e-04 versus 5.3e-04 for seed 1 and 3.0e-04 versus 3.0e-04 for seed 2. Thus the displayed rounded losses include a tie, despite the prose's consistently-smaller description.
